nodes.description: Acquired TTP is an autoimmune disorder in which inhibitory IgG autoantibodies against ADAMTS13 (the VWF-cleaving protease) cause a severe functional deficiency of the enzyme. Unlike the congenital form, the deficiency is not due to germline mutation but to circulating autoantibodies that neutralize or clear the protease.

nodes.description: Caplacizumab (Cablivi) is an anti-von Willebrand factor humanized single-domain immunoglobulin (Nanobody) — a single-variable-domain antibody fragment — that binds the A1 domain of VWF and blocks the VWF-platelet (GPIb) interaction, arresting microthrombus formation despite persistent ADAMTS13 deficiency. Added to plasma exchange and immunosuppression, it speeds platelet normalization and reduces TTP-related death, recurrence, and thromboembolism; the main adverse effect is mucocutaneous bleeding.
